[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Database Migrations with Flask-Migrate in Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Managing database schema changes in a growing web application can quickly become complex. Flask-Migrate is an extension that handles SQLAlchemy database migrations for Flask applications using Alembic. This tutorial will guide you through setting up Flask-Migrate, initializing your migration repository, and applying schema updates safely."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Installation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you begin, ensure you have a Flask application configured with Flask-SQLAlchemy. You need to install Flask-Migrate using pip."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install Flask-Migrate"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Flask-Migrate"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"To initialize Flask-Migrate, you need to import the Migrate class and bind it to your Flask application and SQLAlchemy instance. Typically, this is done in your main application factory or entry point file."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from flask_migrate import Migrate

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'

db = SQLAlchemy(app)
migrate = Migrate(app, db)

class User(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = db.Column(db.String(128))
"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Initializing the Migration Repository"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once Flask-Migrate is integrated, you must initialize the migration environment. Run the following command in your terminal. This creates a migrations folder in your project directory containing the necessary configuration and script templates."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"flask db init"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating and Applying Migrations"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Whenever you alter your database models, you need to generate a new migration script and then apply it to the database."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 1: Generate the migration script using flask db migrate -m "Description of changes"."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 2: Review the generated file inside the migrations/versions directory to ensure the upgrade and downgrade functions are correct."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 3: Apply the migration to the database using flask db upgrade."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"flask db migrate -m "Add User model"
flask db upgrade"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully integrated Flask-Migrate into your Flask application. You can now reliably track schema revisions, collaborate with other developers without risking database conflicts, and roll back changes smoothly when needed."}]
